questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

X takes 0,1,2,3 with probabilities 3/13,1/13,4/13,k. (a) Find k. [3] (b) Find E(X). [3]
questions.summary: X takes 0,1,2,3 with probabilities 3/13,1/13,4/13,k. (a) Find k. [3] (b) Find E(X). [3]
questions.solution: (a) k=5/13. (b) E(X)=(1+8+15)/13=24/13. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider a=(0,3,p) and b=(0,6,18). Find p for which a and b are (a) parallel; [2] (b) perpendicular. [4]
questions.summary: Consider a=(0,3,p) and b=(0,6,18). Find p for which a and b are (a) parallel; [2] (b) perpendicular. [4]
questions.solution: (a) Parallel vectors require b=2a, so 18=2p and p=9. (b) Perpendicular vectors have a·b=0: 18+18p=0, so p=−1. This agrees with the official markscheme.

Consider f(x)=(3x+1)/(x−2), x≠2. (a)(i) Write the vertical asymptote; (ii) find the horizontal asymptote. [3] Let g(x)=x²+4. (b) Find (f∘g)(1). [3]
questions.summary: Consider f(x)=(3x+1)/(x−2), x≠2. (a)(i) Write the vertical asymptote; (ii) find the horizontal asymptote. [3] Let g(x)=x²+4. (b) Find (f∘g)(1). [3]
questions.solution: (a) x=2 and y=3. (b) g(1)=5 and f(5)=16/3. This agrees with the official markscheme.

5. [Maximum mark: 6]

For f(x)=(1−k)x²+x+k, find k for two equal real roots.
questions.summary: For f(x)=(1−k)x²+x+k, find k for two equal real roots.
questions.solution: Δ=1−4k(1−k)=(2k−1)²=0, so k=1/2. This agrees with the official markscheme.
Doubling gives log₄(2−x)²=log₄(13−4x), hence x²=9. Domain restrictions exclude 3, so x=−3. This agrees with the official markscheme.

7. [Maximum mark: 7]

For f(x)=2sinx, 0≤x<2π, line y=−1 meets at A,B. [Sine graph.] (a) Find their x-coordinates. [4] For g(x)=2sin(px), p>0, (b) find greatest p such that g does not meet y=−1. [3]
questions.summary: For f(x)=2sinx, 0≤x<2π, line y=−1 meets at A,B. [Sine graph.] (a) Find their x-coordinates. [4] For g(x)=2sin(px), p>0, (b) find greatest p such that g does not meet y=−1. [3]
questions.solution: (a) 7π/6,11π/6. (b) First possible hit has 2πp=7π/6, so greatest p=7/12. This agrees with the official markscheme.

8. [Maximum mark: 16]

Ten girls’ TV hours have box plot [minimum 8, Q1=15, median 19, Q3=20, maximum a]. (a) Range 16: find a. [2] (b) Find IQR. [2] Total 180. (c) Find mean. [2] Twenty boys have mean 21, σ=3. (d)(i) total; (ii) combined mean. [5] Next week boys watch half as much. (e)(i) mean; (ii) variance. [5]
questions.summary: Ten girls’ TV hours have box plot [minimum 8, Q1=15, median 19, Q3=20, maximum a]. (a) Range 16: find a. [2] (b) Find IQR. [2] Total 180. (c) Find mean. [2] Twenty boys have mean 2
questions.solution: (a) 24. (b) 5. (c) 18. (d) 420 and (180+420)/30=20. (e) Mean 10.5; variance=(1/2)²·9=9/4. This agrees with the official markscheme.

θ is obtuse and sinθ=3/5. (a) Find tanθ. [4] (b) Line L through origin has gradient tanθ; find L. [2] Let f(x)=e^x sinx−3x/4. (c) Find f′. [5] [Graph with tangent M at P parallel to L.] (d) Find x-coordinate of P. [4]
questions.summary: θ is obtuse and sinθ=3/5. (a) Find tanθ. [4] (b) Line L through origin has gradient tanθ; find L. [2] Let f(x)=e^x sinx−3x/4. (c) Find f′. [5] [Graph with tangent M at P parallel t
questions.solution: (a) −3/4. (b) y=−3x/4. (c) By the product rule, f′(x)=e^x sinx+e^x cosx−3/4=e^x(sinx+cosx)−3/4. (d) Parallel gradients give e^x(sinx+cosx)−3/4=−3/4, hence sinx+cosx=0 and x=3π/4. This agrees with the official markscheme.

10. [Maximum mark: 14]

Let y=(x³+x)^(3/2). (a) Find dy/dx. [3] (b) Hence find ∫(3x²+1)√(x³+x)dx. [3] Let f=√(x³+x), g=6x−3x²+√(x³+x). [Diagram: region R between f,g,y-axis,x=1.] (c) Give an area expression. [2] (d) Find exact area. [6]

questions.solution: (a) (3/2)(x³+x)^(1/2)(3x²+1). (b) (2/3)(x³+x)^(3/2)+C. (c) ∫₀¹(6x−3x²)dx. (d) [3x²−x³]₀¹=2. This agrees with the official markscheme.
